record.paper_title: Symmetric Functions in Superspace: A Compendium of Results and Open Problems (Including a SageMath Worksheet)
record.context_brief: Evaluation symmetry for normalized Macdonald superpolynomials
record.original_question: For superpartitions Λ and Ω of the same degree, define the specialization u_Λ by x_{w_Λ(i)}=q^{-Λ^*_i}t^{i-1}, and define the normalized Macdonald superpolynomial ~P_Λ = P_Λ / P_Λ(u_{(δ^m;)}). Is the symmetry relation ~P_Λ(u_Ω)=~P_Ω(u_Λ) always true?

evidence.quote: The specialization u_Λ gives the variables x1, . . . , xN the values (4.65) u_Λ : x_{w_Λ(i)} = q^{−Λ^*_i} t^{i−1}, i = 1, 2, . . . , N,
We now define the following normalized version of P_Λ as (4.68) ~P_Λ = P_Λ/P_Λ(u_{(δ^m;)}), which is such that ~P_Λ(ǫ_{q,t}) = 1.
Conjecture 4.2 – (Symmetry). [41] For any superpartitions Λ, Ω of the same degree, we have (4.69) ~P_Λ(u_Ω) = ~P_Ω(u_Λ).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in superspace: the polynomial ring in commuting variables x_1,...,x_N together with anticommuting variables θ_1,...,θ_N (θ_iθ_j = -θ_jθ_i). A superpartition Λ = (Λ^a; Λ^s) of fermionic degree m and total degree n consists of a strictly decreasing partition Λ^a = (Λ_1,...,Λ_m) with Λ_i ≥ 0 and a usual partition Λ^s, with |Λ^a|+|Λ^s| = n. To Λ associate the composition Λ^* obtained by reading the parts of Λ^a then Λ^s, and let w_Λ be the unique permutation of minimal length such that w_Λ·Λ^* gives the parts arranged in the canonical labeling associated with Λ.

For parameters q,t, let P_Λ = P_Λ(x_1,...,x_N; θ_1,...,θ_N; q,t) denote the Macdonald symmetric superpolynomial indexed by Λ (the unique element, up to normalization, characterized by triangularity with respect to dominance on superpartitions and orthogonality with respect to the Macdonald scalar product in superspace).

Define the specialization u_Λ on the variables x_1,...,x_N by
   x_{w_Λ(i)} = q^{-Λ^*_i} t^{i-1},   i = 1,2,...,N,
and the normalization
   ~P_Λ := P_Λ / P_Λ(u_{(δ^m;)}),
where (δ^m;) denotes the staircase superpartition (m-1, m-2, ..., 1, 0; ) of fermionic degree m. With this normalization ~P_Λ evaluated at the standard point ε_{q,t} equals 1.

Question: For every pair of superpartitions Λ, Ω of the same total degree (and the same fermionic degree), does the evaluation symmetry
   ~P_Λ(u_Ω) = ~P_Ω(u_Λ)
hold identically as a rational function of q and t?
artifact.status_search_result: A search for recent work on Macdonald superpolynomials, including papers on evaluation of nonsymmetric Macdonald superpolynomials at special points (2021), m-symmetric functions and positivity (2022), and Macdonald polynomials for super-partitions (2024), did not surface a definitive proof or disproof of the evaluation-symmetry conjecture ~P_Λ(u_Ω) = ~P_Ω(u_Λ) for symmetric Macdonald superpolynomials. Related evaluation/duality results exist in the nonsymmetric setting, but the symmetric superspace evaluation symmetry appears to remain a conjecture in the literature reviewed.

status_evidence.title: Evaluation of Nonsymmetric Macdonald Superpolynomials at Special Points
status_evidence.snippet: Determines values of a subclass of nonsymmetric Macdonald superpolynomials at special points (1,t,t^2,...) and (1,t^{-1},t^{-2},...).
status_evidence.claim: Recent work treats specialization/evaluation of nonsymmetric Macdonald superpolynomials, but does not establish the symmetric evaluation-symmetry conjecture.

status_evidence.title: m-Symmetric functions, non-symmetric Macdonald polynomials and positivity conjectures
status_evidence.snippet: Develops m-symmetric Macdonald theory connected to superspace and positivity conjectures.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent developments focus on positivity and m-symmetric framework rather than proving the evaluation symmetry.

status_evidence.title: Macdonald polynomials for super-partitions
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces super-Macdonald polynomials via orthogonality relations on extended super-Young diagrams.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2024) extension does not announce a proof of the symmetric evaluation symmetry conjecture in superspace.
